items.pitch: The whole solid-apps suite loads its auth layer from an unpinned, un-SRI'd <script src="https://unpkg.com/xlogin"> (xlogin supplies the credentialed authFetch used for every private-pod read/write), so one hijacked or broken 'latest' publish of xlogin runs with full pod credentials in ~18 apps at once — pin an exact version with an SRI integrity hash, or vendor the file the way intents does.
items.evidence: Unversioned, integrity-less `<script src="https://unpkg.com/xlogin">` in index.html across the suite: notifications, camera, gallery, webacl, tunnel, peer, wallet, health, nutrition (batch I) AND weather, maps, messages, contacts, kanban, bookmarks, notes, calendar, split (batch J); taproot loads it too. maps also pulls leaflet@1.9.4 and taproot qrcodejs from CDN without SRI. intents is the only app that vendors it.

items.pitch: nexus's HTML/markdown sanitizer strips script/style/iframe tags but leaves inline event-handler attributes (onerror/onclick) and javascript: URLs intact before assigning doc.body.innerHTML, so any fetched web page or pod document (e.g. ) executes JS in the app origin with the user's authenticated fetch (which can PUT to the pod) — strip on* attributes and javascript: hrefs in the same sanitize pass.
items.evidence: index.html:346 removes only 'script,style,link,meta,iframe,object,embed,base', then index.html:352 w.docEl.innerHTML=doc.body.innerHTML; same gap in renderMarkdown (index.html:326/333); authenticated PUT at index.html:431

items.pitch: taproot is a mainnet Bitcoin wallet that reads the raw secp256k1 private key from the pod into page memory, yet loads its JS from mutable CDN URLs — unpkg.com/xlogin (unversioned) and cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/davidshimjs/qrcodejs (unversioned), no SRI on any script — so a hijacked package release can exfiltrate the key and drain funds; pin exact versions and add integrity hashes or vendor the scripts.
items.evidence: index.html:63-65 (unpkg.com/xlogin unpinned, qrcodejs unpinned, tapscript@1.4.6 pinned but no integrity) + index.html:119-133 loadSecret() reading /private/privkey.jsonld into JS memory

items.pitch: A crafted share link (?key=txo:<network>:<txid>:<vout>) is auto-imported on page load and the attacker-controlled txid/network are written into the voucher-card HTML unescaped, giving reflected XSS in an app that holds Bitcoin private keys (key exfiltration); run txid/network through escHtml() before interpolating.
items.evidence: vouchers.js:944 interpolates ${v.txid} into an href and link text unescaped, and :929 renders ${(v.network||'').toUpperCase()} unescaped; init() at :1211 auto-imports ?key= via importKey(), which does no hex validation on txid/network. escHtml() exists (used for privkey at :951) but is not applied here.

items.pitch: Revoking an agent flips its status to 'revoked' but leaves every previously-shared card's .acl still granting that did:nostr key acl:Read (the toast even tells the user to manually re-open each shared card), so a supposedly revoked key keeps reading ID/payment/credential cards — on revoke, iterate ITEMS whose sharedWith includes the agentId and rewrite their ACLs without it.
items.evidence: solid-apps/wallet/app.js:219-222 — toggleAgent() only calls saveItem(it) on the agent card itself; writeAcl (app.js:124-129) runs solely for the item being saved, so cards listing the revoked agent in wallet:sharedWith keep their #shared acl:Read authorization (app.js:109). The toast at line 221 admits it: 'Agent revoked — re-open any shared card to drop its access'.

items.pitch: Phone-book imports (third parties' names, emails, phone numbers) are written to the world-readable /public/contacts/ container and the repo's own open issue #1 already accepts the fix — implement it by pointing BOOK at a /private/ container (as weather/maps/messages do) or seeding an owner-only ACL.

Siblings store equivalent data privately (weather/app.js:8, maps/app.js:9, messages/app.js:14).

items.pitch: follow()/unfollow() silently destroy the user's whole follow list when the kind-3 fetch returns null — pool.get() resolves null after its 8s timeout or when the list isn't on the default relays, publishContacts then signs a fresh kind-3 with 0-1 p-tags and empty content, and the null is cached page-wide so every click repeats it — refuse to publish when the previous contact list is null (or require explicit first-list confirmation).
items.evidence: contacts.js:25-34 — myContacts caches cache.promise = pool.get({kinds:[3],authors:[key]}) which can resolve null; contacts.js:42-49 — tags = [...(prevEvent?.tags ?? [])], content = prevEvent?.content ?? ''; contacts.js:60-70 — follow/unfollow publish the result; pool/pool.js:209-228 — list() resolves whatever arrived within 8s, get() returns events[0] ?? null. README ironically promises it 'won't wipe your follows' metadata like careless clients do'.

items.pitch: login.html injects the stored profile name into innerHTML without escaping ('Continue as '+label) while index.html escapes the same value, so an attacker-controlled Nostr display name persisted to shared localStorage executes as HTML in the login page (DOM XSS on a page handling keys) — wrap label in esc().
items.evidence: login.html:118 — $('continueWrap').innerHTML = `<button ... id=contBtn>Continue as ${label}</button>...` with label=(mem().name) unescaped; mem().name is written unescaped in index.html:390 (from Nostr profile p.name fetched from a relay) and index.html:574-575 (from ?name= query param), both stored under the shared localStorage key 'bridges.v0'. Every other innerHTML sink in bridges (index.html:396,459,556) uses esc(); login.html:118 is the lone outlier.
